card.name: Words just before a 'not enough' phrase
card.fires_on: A noun or auxiliary word that ends a subject phrase and is followed by a negative or insufficiency statement, such as 'not enough' or 'not adequate'. Also appears on other mid-phrase words in general web text.

modes.label: Before insufficiency
modes.description: Subject word right before 'not be enough' or 'not an adequate'.
modes.example: Raising level<< might>> not be enough, so separate that hit

modes.label: Noun ending a phrase
modes.description: Last noun of a phrase like 'in the wild' or 'naked eye' that sets up a contrast.
modes.example: With no further protection in the<< wild>>, these species are predicted to become extinct

card.writes: It favors Chinese words meaning inconvenient, not good enough or insufficient, which suggests it pushes toward negative or 'not enough' continuations.
card.plain: It fires on words that come just before a statement that something is not enough or not suitable.
